short_text: Fazalhaq Farooqi to Markram, no run
commentary: short of length and slanting across, Markram nicely on top of the bounce as he defends
pre_text:
Out come Markram and de Kock. We're all set for live action. Farooqi with the new ball with his left-arm pace. 


Less than three weeks ago, the only thing Tristan Stubbs was concerned about was winning the SA20 final. He knew he wasn't part of the T20 World Cup mix, and had made peace with it. But the universe had other plans. Firdose Moonda caught up with him.



The XIs for you

SA: Markram, de Kock, Rickleton, Brewis, Miller, Stubbs, Jansen, Linde, Rabada, Maharaj, Ngidi

Afghanistan: Gurbaz, Zadran, Naib, Atal, Rasooli, Omarzai, Nabi, Rashid, Noor, Farooqi, Mujeeb

10.30am  Heads says Rashid Khan, heads it is.  Afghanistan opt to bowl.  "Important to collectively put an effort towards winning," he says. "IPL home ground for me, wicket gets better. Need to improve our powerplay batting, also need to bowl better in the middle overs. Missed our lines and lengths against New Zealand."

Zia-ur Rahman misses out, Noor Ahmad comes in. 

Markram says South Africa would've bowled, but hope to put up runs and apply the squeeze later on. "Decent in our opening game, important to keep raising the bar.  One change: George Linde in for Corbin Bosch" 

In addition to your feedback and comments that I'll try and publish as frequently as possible, you can also join Sidharth Monga on our Live Report for all the analysis real time.


Niazai opens our comments today: "It's like a quarter-final for us. We're all praying in Afghanistan."

10.12am  The one question that lingered much after Afghanistan lost to New Zealand in Chennai was: why didn't Noor Ahmad play? It confounded many, including Ian Bishop as he looks ahead to this match on ESPNcricinfo Time Out.

Firdose Moonda has taken her seat, but the same can't be said about the fans. "Very very very few people in here," she pings. 

"Afghanistan have been in a huddle for a long time. Linde, Maharaj, Nortje and Maphaka on the practice pitch but that was not an indication of anything last time."

Weather-wise, Firdose says it "feels like a much hotter day already than the previous few."

10am  Hello and a warm welcome to ESPNcricinfo's continued coverage of the men's T20 World Cup. 

The first of today's triple-header takes us to Ahmedabad with Afghanistan hoping to stay alive in the competition without the calculators as they face South Africa in a Group D fixture. 

I'm Shashank Kishore. and I'll be with you right through this contest.  Hemant Brar's preview  should set you nicely while I get a cup of coffee.

short_text: Ngidi to Mohammad Nabi, no run
commentary: late tail in, this one squeezes off an inside edge to short fire. For a second, Nabi wasn't sure where the ball went.
into the blockhole and honing in towards leg-stump, Nabi somehow manages to get some bat on it, scampers a single
pre_text: Srashta : "Gotta remind people of the famous Dean Jones incident where he had Ambrose take off his wrist bands - the Aussies dint like what came after."

commentary: another dipping full toss, worked past midwicket for a single

short_text: Jansen to Azmatullah Omarzai, no run
commentary: beaten as he looks to flay that behind point. He went cutter into the pitch as expected first up
looks to back away and slap it straight back. No timing as the ball rolls to long-off
flicked to short fine, direct hit at the striker's end by Ngidi, but Azmat is well in
important boundary! Too full and down leg, Amzat gets enough bat on it to flick it fine and past the man inside the ring.
carved over cover, down to the boundary rider. This one tailed away late, but timed very nicely.
that has been clobbered over cover! Tracer-bullet stuff. Hit really, really hard. No chance for the sweeper to come around in time. Sweet contact.

is that the match? Nabi's gone. Linde tossed one up on leg stump from over the wicket, Nabi looks to go against the turn and heave across the line but ends up slicing it to point. Markram at no point looked like missing that. Linde got that to dip on the batter and spin sharply. Terrific bowling.
dismissal: Mohammad Nabi c Markram b Linde 5 (16m 6b 0x4 0x6) SR: 83.33

commentary: pushed into the covers for a single
leading edge but it eludes the bowler despite the dive, down to long-off
bad ball, picked away for four! All Rashid had to do was lend direction with the sweep and he did so to perfection.
cut away nicely, Jansen runs to his right from short third and them tumbles around to stop the ball
gets leg side of the ball and eases it into the covers for a single
goes pace off on a length again, forced to deep cover for a single
hammered for four! Rashid was expecting the short ball. And he set himself up superbly to pick that slower bouncer on middle into the gap at deep midwicket

short_text: Rabada to Rashid Khan, no run
commentary: a huge shriek of 'oh no no no' from Rashid as he slaps this slower length ball straight to cover

he' s turning it on and in some style is Rashid! Attempted Yorker to the base of off-stump but Rashid brings the bat down in time to lend direction as he opens the bat face to steer it past short third.  Remember Iyer off Bumrah? Somewhat similar. Wow.
heaved into the leg side, they'll pinch a single
toe-ends this alap to point, they'll take a single.
this slower full toss has been picked away down leg to beat a diving short fine leg. Wonder if he's become too predictable now with the dipping full toss - it's all the batters are expecting
turns this low full toss towards deep midwicket

short_text: Ngidi to Rashid Khan, no run
commentary: beaten as he tries to open the bat face to steer this behind point. Got just enough dip on it to sneak underneath the bat
cutter into the pitch, awkward bounce on it as Rashid somehow manages to tuck it to the leg side.

ice-cool Stubbs has pulled off a stunner at long-on under pressure! Azmat lofted that high and handsome using all his might to get power and elevation against that slower ball into the pitch. Stubbs got his hands on it, but realised he was going over. So threw the ball back in, and then rebalanced himself inside the boundary to grab it on the second attempt. He wasn't meant to be here, but has Stubbs changed the course of the game with this catch or what?
dismissal: Azmatullah Omarzai c Stubbs b Ngidi 22 (30m 17b 3x4 0x6) SR: 129.41

short_text: Ngidi to Mujeeb Ur Rahman, no run
commentary: somehow manages to keep out that full delivery. Six and a wicket, what an over.
slapped down the ground towards long-off as they scamper back for the second
pre_text: Get the sense it's Rashid v South Africa now.

commentary: slants it too far across the batter, wide called. Rashid was looking to move across
pre_text: OxTiger : "What a match! What a clutch performance from Ngidi! Pipping both Rabada and Rashid in the same match! Who woulda thunk?"

commentary: he's given it all his might, ends up slicing this up and over the infield as it dribbles towards the third man boundary, two more.  But Linde is down with a cramp, has he? He's clutching his right knee.  He's off the park. Substitute fielder comes in.

he has bludgeoned this straight and hard, for the longest time it seems like it'll elude long on, but David Miller sprinted around to his left and threw himself full stretch to firstly get two the ball and then hold on with full focus as he put in the slide.  Catches win matches, Miller has surely done it for South Africa. Could well be the turning point.
dismissal: Rashid Khan c Miller b Jansen 20 (17m 12b 3x4 0x6) SR: 166.66

commentary: good, clean strike down the ground for six! Noor belted that as if he was having fun at the driving range. Proper slot ball, Noor belted that nearly a 100 metres. Game on or what? Wowwwwwwww

short_text: Jansen to Noor Ahmad, no run
commentary: slaps it straight to cover point. Dot to end.

direct hit from Jansen as he grabs the ball on his followthrough with Mujeeb well short of the crease. There was no single there as Noor didn't time it at all. Slight collision between the non-striker and Jansen, but he managed to gather himself to hit bull's eye
dismissal: Mujeeb Ur Rahman run out 0 (8m 1b 0x4 0x6) SR: 0

short_text: Rabada to Noor Ahmad, 1 no ball
commentary: oh, dear! Rabada has bowled a no-ball that gives Afghanistan a lifeline! South Africa were celebrating as Noor couldn't time this and could only hit it as far as cover. But the siren goes off, and it's now a free-hit for Afghanistan.
slips this full and down leg, Noor looks to flick, this is called wide. Still six balls left, 11 needed. Free-hit stays

short_text: Rabada to Noor Ahmad, no run
commentary: shelled down to long-off, dropped by Jansen.  That was an absolute dolly.  But again, didn't matter. Run saved?
Noooooooooor! What are you made of? Makes room and takes on the short ball that sat up right in his swinging arc. Clears deep backward square. What a sensational hit.

short_text: Rabada to Noor Ahmad, no run
commentary: full and tailing in, Noor works it down to long-on. Refuses the run but Farooqi was more than halfway down when he was sent back

short_text: Rabada to Noor Ahmad, (no ball) 2 runs
commentary: goes straight down the ground, hacks it into the leg side towards wide long-on, they scamper back for a second....but wait, Rabada has bowled another no-ball.

short_text: Rabada to Noor Ahmad, 1 run, OUT
commentary: drilled down to wide long-off, as they scamper a second. The throw comes in on the bounce to Rabada who stretches back to break the bails at the bowler's end with Farooqi a millimetre short of the crease. Third umpire needs just two replays to confirm what Afghanistan feared. There was one legit delivery remaining. Could they have tried to take it to the final ball? South Africa will believe they've got out of jail. This was done and dusted when a wicket fell first ball, but for that no-ball. Afghanistan then came storming back.  And now here we are, going into the tournament's first Super over.
